source_user: Two serving systems claim different tokens/s. Design a reproducible comparison. Scenario variant 293: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: freeze model revision, tokenizer, precision, hardware, topology, prompt/generation distributions, concurrency, warmup, stopping rules, and telemetry; publish raw request traces.
corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 293, make the comparison reproducible before interpreting tokens/s. Assume both systems can run the same model revision, tokenizer, precision, decoding parameters, stop rules, and quality target; if not, disclose the incompatibility and do not claim a like-for-like result. Pin runtime and serving versions, hardware, topology, clocks and power limits, request corpus and prompt/output-length distributions, concurrency, offered load, admission, batching, cache state, network path, warmup, duration, and inclusion/stopping rules.

Use one falsifiable mechanism hypothesis: after these controls, scheduler overhead (or a named kernel/runtime difference) causes the residual throughput gap. Disconfirm it if the effect is inside a predeclared practical margin, reverses across randomized paired trials, or vanishes when that mechanism is controlled. Reuse immutable request IDs, randomize A/B order, run repeated paired crossovers at several load/concurrency points, and report incomplete or failed requests rather than selecting the best run.

Define metrics with numerator, denominator, and units: input-token/s, generated-token/s, and accepted-token/s where applicable. Separately report end-to-end throughput and queue, admission, dispatch, time-to-first-token, inter-token, and completion latency, stating whether network, retries, cancellations, padding, speculative/rejected tokens, and idle time are included. Capture synchronized request timestamps, configuration/workload hashes, raw traces, and analysis code. Report p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU/CPU/memory/power/thermal utilization, queue depth, batch sizes, errors/timeouts/retries, correctness, and output quality with uncertainty.

Expected confounders include cache warmth, length mix and early stopping, tokenizer accounting, batching/admission, autoscaling, contention, thermal throttling, clock drift, network variance, implementation maturity, and missing telemetry. If traces cannot separate queue from service time, limit causal conclusions. Roll out only through a fixed-traffic canary with predeclared quality, correctness, error, latency, resource, and telemetry SLOs; fail closed to the known-good system on threshold breach, safety or quality regression, missing telemetry, or unexplained variance, and preserve artifacts for review.
